Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. Democrats Scott Colombe has won election to the U.S. Senate from Mississippi according to a race call by the Associated Press, nearly defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, NPR's Elena Moore reports.
This race ultimately came down to just a few thousand votes, taking over a week to call as election officials counted outstanding ballots. It's a historic Democratic upset and a major blow to Republicans.
Even in a year where Democrats had momentum, the Mississippi Senate race was not expected to be a toss-up heading into Election Day. It's long been a ruby-red state. Just two years ago, President Trump carried Mississippi by double digits.
Now, Colombe will be the first Democrat to represent the state in the Senate in more than 40 years. He'll also be Mississippi's first black U.S. Senator since Reconstruction. Elena Moore, NPR News.
A judge has rejected the BBC's request to dismiss President Trump's defamation case against the British broadcaster. Trump alleges a BBC documentary defamed him by splicing together his remarks before the January 6th Capitol attack, and bears David Falkenflick reports.
The BBC argues Trump hadn't alleged any harm. He withdrew claims of business losses and is seeking to avoid having to share records of his financial holdings and dealings.
And the BBC says the 2024 documentary, aired two weeks before the presidential elections, wasn't shown in this country, much less Florida, where the case was filed. That failed to impress the presiding judge, Jeffrey Kuntz, who was appointed by the President and is overseeing the case.
He said the BBC's editing gave the mistaken impression that Trump called for violence. And the judge said the timing so close to the election bolsters the defamation claim. Evaluating the case's merits, Judge Kuntz wrote, would fall to another day. David Falkenflick, NPR News.
The Board of Peace, created by President Trump to run Gaza, is urging Israel to immediately authorize essential temporary shelters in Gaza, calling the crisis, quote, "an immediate humanitarian emergency." NPR's Anas Baba reports.
The board's warning follows the sea. Israel maintains it has been working in recent months on a winter preparedness plan with international organizations. But aid agencies say they have warned for months that the restrictions on essential winter supplies are blocking life-saving work.
Here is the honest spokesperson James Elder on coordination with an Israeli military agency called Kogat.
Plans are drawn, money's raised, equipment is ready. But just recently Kogat rejected the project. Old argument, can't bring in the equipment needed on security grounds.
Elder called on Israeli authorities to allow rehabilitation work to go through before, quote, "in Gaza." Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza City.
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large prisoner exchange during U.S. mediated talks, but no major breakthroughs were announced in efforts to end the war that began nearly five years ago.
The two-day session in Abu Dhabi was the first meeting in nine months. U.S. officials are now heading to Moscow to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
A building in Brooklyn has collapsed and the fire department says people are trapped in the rubble. The New York City Fire Department says at least one person was killed.
News helicopter footage shows dozens of firefighters scouring the debris. The collapse happened next to a site where construction had been occurring.
The Trump administration has announced plans to ease regulations for cattle grazing on federal public lands. NPR's Kirk Sigler reports it's an effort to boost domestic beef production that environmentalists say is misguided.
President Trump's interior and agriculture secretaries have proposed rules that would expand the number of grazing permits available to cattle ranchers on public rangelands in the West, as well as cement a uniform grazing fee of $1.61 that ranchers will owe the government for each cow they graze on an allotment.
The proposed regulations are the latest move by this administration to try to bring down beef prices in the long term. Environmentalists are quick to point out that the majority of American beef is now raised in the Midwest, largely on feedlots, not Western public land because it costs a lot more per cow there and has to be subsidized by taxpayers.
Western ranchers, meanwhile, support the proposed cheaper grazing fees, saying they pay out of pocket for fencing and irrigation, which is rising due to inflation. Kirk Sigler in PR News, Boise.
A European spacecraft has begun inspections of an asteroid targeted by NASA four years ago in a planetary defense test. The European Space Agency says that the HERA spacecraft is studying didymos and its moonlit dimorphose. NASA's DART spacecraft slammed into dimorphose in 2022 to see whether such a move might help save Earth one day from a killer space rock. This is NPR News.
